Saint John area educators among those honoured by PM

Bryan Tait October 8, 2026 5:04 am

A trio of Greater Saint John educators are being recognized for their work.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:26
Instaread

Kerri Titus of Harbour View High, Tanisha Thompson from Fundy Shores School and Avril Wood-Toner from the YMCA of Southwestern New Brunswick have all received certificates of achievement from the Prime Minister’s Awards.

The awards celebrate educators who demonstrate outstanding leadership and exceptional education practices.

They also show a commitment to preparing students to succeed in Canada’s innovation-based economy.

“Education is one of the most powerful forces for transforming our country and shaping our shared future,” Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statemen.

“Teachers are at the heart of that work, helping the next generation to learn, to lead and to build a stronger Canada.” 

Kerri Titus

Titus received a Certificate of Achievement in the Teaching Excellence category.

She teaches science, chemistry and biology to students in grades 9 to 12 at the Saint John school.

Titus’s biography on the awards site described her as an “(e)mpathetic, creative science teacher” who helps her students understand challenging ideas by breaking them down in meaningful and manageable ways.

She creates inclusive labs, adapts materials and supports students of all backgrounds so they all have a chance to succeed.

A vice-principal at Harbour View said Titus sees potential where others see barriers.

“When one of my struggling students is fortunate enough to have her, I know they will the odds and achieve success,” that vice-principal said.

Tanisha Thompson

Thompson teaches Grade 1 and 2 at Fundy Shores School in Dipper Harbour, covering all subjects.

According to her biography, she brings together literacy, technology and social-emotional learning to create classrooms where every child can succeed.

She designs hands-on learning experiences that use coding, robotics, storytelling and design.

“She allowed my kids to be themselves,” a colleague and parent of a student told the awards committee.

“Appreciating their unique personalities and needs, and introduced them to coding, woodworking and gardening, broadening their horizons in ways I could never have imagined.”

Avril Wood-Toner

Wood-Toner has spent more than 30 years in early childhood education.

In her role at the YMCA of Southwestern New Brunswick, she brings education, health and social services together in neighbourhoods, so families face fewer barriers.

Her approach fosters curiosity, a sense of belonging and strong relationships.

“Her passion ignited a movement,” an early learning consultant told the awards committee.

“Her impact will continue to ripple for years to come.”
